paper_id: Cheng et al. - 2008 - Sweep coverage with mobile sensors
title: Sweep Coverage with Mobile Sensors
motivation: Many applications require only periodic monitoring of POIs (patrol inspection), not continuous full coverage; existing static coverage is inefficient and wasteful for such dynamic requirements
problem_framing: Define sweep coverage where each POI must be covered at least once every t time units; formulate min-sensor sweep-coverage problem: find minimum number of mobile sensors to satisfy all sweep period requirements
key_insight: Sweep coverage enables covering many POIs with few mobile sensors by exploiting time-variant coverage; the problem's non-locality (no sensor can locally determine global coverage) necessitates distributed coordination via epidemic information exchange
method_signature: CSWEEP: TSP PTAS route + partition into L0 pieces, each sensor patrols one piece; DSWEEP: distributed with epidemic sweep table exchange and urgency-based next POI selection
evaluation_criteria: Cumulative distribution of actual sweep period vs required; fraction of reliable POIs meeting requirements; comparison against RAND randomized scheme
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: min-sensor sweep-coverage is NP-hard and cannot be approximated within factor 2; centralized CSWEEP not scalable; DSWEEP provides only best-effort, not guaranteed coverage
evidence_for_taste: cannot be approximated within a factor of 2
none of the distributed local algorithms can guarantee
CSWEEP is not scalable and adaptive
thinking_moves: Reduce sweep coverage to TSP for hardness proof
Characterize problem non-locality to justify distributed design
Adapt robotics sweep concept to sensor networks via epidemic routing
Build distributed algorithm from bottom-up: information exchange then local decision
